decision_conditions:
<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="line-height: normal;">Noise and
Residential Amenity Impact<o:p></o:p></p><p>

</p><p class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: normal;">Insufficient information has been
provided to assess the likely noise impacts arising from the proposed nursery
use, including noise associated with outdoor play areas, child activity,
vehicle movements, arrivals and departures, and the cumulative effects of the
continued operation of the synagogue. In the absence of a robust noise
assessment and appropriate mitigation measures, the Local Planning Authority
cannot be satisfied that the proposal would safeguard the amenities of
neighbouring residential occupiers. The proposal is therefore contrary to
Policy D14 (Noise) of the London Plan 2021 and Policy GR1 (Achieving a High
Standard of Development) of the Harrow Local Plan 2021–2041, which seek to
ensure that development does not result in unacceptable impacts on residential
amenity.<font face="Arial, sans-serif"><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><o:p></o:p></span></font></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">Cumulative Impact<o:p></o:p></p><p>

</p><p class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: normal;">Insufficient information has been
provided to demonstrate how the proposed nursery use, accommodating up to 60
children together with staff, would successfully coexist alongside the
established synagogue use operating from the site. In the absence of detailed
information regarding the intensity of occupation, hours of operation, site
management arrangements, shared use of facilities, access arrangements and peak
demand periods, the Council is unable to adequately assess the cumulative
impacts arising from the concurrent operation of both uses. The proposal
therefore fails to demonstrate that the development would function
satisfactorily without adverse impacts on site operation, neighbouring
occupiers or local infrastructure, contrary to Policies GG3, D3 and S1 of the
London Plan 2021 and Policies GR1 (Achieving a High Standard of Development)
and SI1 (Safeguarding and Securing Social Infrastructure) of the Harrow Local
Plan 2021–2041.<font face="Arial, sans-serif"><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><o:p></o:p></span></font></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">Highway Impact<o:p></o:p></p><p>

</p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">Insufficient
information has been submitted to enable a full assessment of the impact of the
proposed nursery use on the local highway network. In particular, no
satisfactory transport evidence has been provided to assess likely vehicle
trips, pick-up and drop-off activity, parking demand, servicing arrangements,
cycle parking provision and the cumulative transport impacts associated with
the continued operation of the synagogue. In the absence of such information,
the Local Planning Authority cannot be satisfied that the proposal would not
result in adverse impacts on highway safety, traffic flow or parking conditions
in the surrounding area. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies T4
(Assessing and Mitigating Transport Impacts), T6 (Car Parking) and T7
(Deliveries, Servicing and Construction) of the London Plan 2021, and Policies
M1 (Sustainable Transport) and &nbsp;M2
(Parking) of the Harrow Local Plan 2021–2041<span style="font-size:
12.0pt;font-family:&quot;Arial&quot;,sans-serif;mso-fareast-font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;">.<o:p></o:p></span></p>
description: change of use of the existing youth hall in association with Pinner Synagogue (Class F2(b)) to a Nursery (Class E (f)).
